decisions.reason: As a flagship reusable crate closely aligned with the firm's sustainability direction, it still offers strategic option value and is unlikely to be withdrawn absent clear evidence of poor demand.

A foldable large container line with several models and dedicated presentation fits the firm's core logistics-packaging business and is worth keeping because its market potential remains broad while carrying costs are likely moderate.
A stackable plastic crate line is a core adjacent product for many customer segments, so the firm would likely retain it as a low-cost option within its established reusable packaging portfolio.
The medium-duty rackable pallet line extends the firm's pallet offering in a familiar application area, making it more sensible to keep than drop while uncertainty about long-term uptake remains.
The spill-retention pallet is more niche and was somewhat less prominently shown later, but it still complements the pallet range and likely costs little enough to keep as a specialized option.

The plastic pallet with load retainers appears narrower and somewhat de-emphasized, yet it remains close to the firm's capabilities and customer needs, so management would more likely keep than drop it for now.
